data.title: ‘Scots are the kindest people on earth!’ Meet the Americans moving to Scotland
data.description: Since Donald Trump’s re-election in 2024, there has been a 63% rise in Americans renting properties in Scotland. Politics is one reason – but there are many other surprising motivations … Four years ago, when Tammi Gaw, a 50-year-old property adviser, moved from Washington DC to Glasgow with her Scottish partner, friends and family laughed at her. “People back home kept asking me: ‘Ha ha, why would you want to move to Scotland, where it rains all the time?’ Now those same people are asking me: ‘Hey, how do I move there?’” They are not alone. According to data from Rightmove , 28% of inquiries from Americans about buying a home in the UK are about Scotland, a larger number than for London. And a recent survey from lettings platform Goodlord reported a 63% rise in the number of Americans renting properties in Scotland since Donald Trump’s re-election in November 2024. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A completely unique opportunity’: the secretive process that will decide the BBC’s future
data.description: Every decade, the BBC’s continued existence must be secured through an elaborate multi-year negotiation with the government. But what does charter renewal actually involve – and will it secure the BBC’s long-term future? In a temperature-controlled room in a suburb of Reading, the basis of the BBC’s existence is kept in a flat, square, faded navy case, the size of a large pizza box. Inside is a stack of vellum – calfskin, pounded until it forms a milky and translucent paper that is supposed to last for thousands of years. The queen’s red wax seal is secured to its base with red and gold cord. The pages are strapped down with two strips of white elastic, more PE kit than Buckingham Palace. The document is unique. Like hundreds of other British organisations, the BBC was founded via a Royal Charter, granted by the monarch of the day. But unlike Oxford colleges, the British Film Institute, or the Worshipful Company of Makers of Playing Cards, the BBC was given an expiry date. When the British Broadcasting Corporation was founded, in the 1920s, radio was seen as such an uncertain, risky technology that the government only gave it a 10-year guarantee, after which it would have to seek a new charter. Continue reading...

data.title: Ridiculed by the press – and now King Charles is joining in. Sorry, Harry, but what did you expect? | Emma Brockes
data.description: The Sussexes must have hoped for a warm welcome. Then they read the king’s delicately savage letter about ‘private citizens’ As welcome-back-to-Britain gestures go, the lord chamberlain’s letter , sent on behalf of King Charles on Monday to remind Harry, Meghan and everyone watching that they’re still “private citizens”, was so perfect as to restore me to monarchism. After six years in the wilderness, what greater comfort for Prince Harry than to find himself, once again, in the familiar waters of this country’s passive aggression, being attacked by his father via the merciless phrase “fully respected”, and provoking from the prince a coded up-yours in the form of his publicly stated “surprise”. Well, it’s up there with better cheese, bread and the NHS, isn’t it?! Even the most Eurocentric American can’t match us for this kind of subtextual bare-knuckle fight. Before we get into what else the returnees may be enjoying this month, let’s fully excavate the letter’s encrypted hostility. First, the king’s repeated use of the words “personal” and “private” – as in “the charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity” – is so intense, so heavy handed, as to go beyond merely calling his younger son a civilian and come perilously close to the ultimate insult, “middle class”. Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: ‘He goes to the dark side’: behind the scenes on the Shaun the Sheep horror movie
data.description: Aardman’s hero is back in The Beast of Mossy Bottom – a terrifying tale of frankenfood, pitchfork-wielding villagers and a monster with suspiciously stiff orange hair. Our writer meets its makers and moulds her very own Shaun The Aztec West industrial estate in Bristol was opened by Margaret Thatcher in December 1989. One hundred and sixty acres of breeze block and mirrored glass, it is home to about 7,000 employees and 100 companies, including EDF, EE, HSBC, Co-op Legal and Spandex. It has its own gym, spa, church and morgue. Step inside Unit 1410, though, and bucolic England is magically restored. A farm complete with sheep. Rolling fields in autumn colours. A small parish town boasting post office, war memorial, chippy. It looks lush. But before you hit up Rightmove, I should say: Mossingham is only two feet tall. And plasticine. It’s January 2026 and Aardman animations are about halfway through production on Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom. The 300-odd staff in this shed are full speed ahead – which means each of the 30 animators is rattling out almost two seconds of footage a day . Continue reading...

data.description: Funding cuts in 2025 left women, children, older and displaced people hard hit, with 64m fewer people receiving aid The humanitarian aid system is crumbling as funding shrinks, pressures increase and governments not only fail to protect civilians but are increasingly responsible for endangering them, a new report warned on Thursday as figures revealed 64 million fewer people received aid last year. data.title: How the fate of a small furry animal reveals the ecological tragedy of Israel’s war on Lebanon | Hisham Younes
data.description: The Syrian rock hyrax depends on the fragile landscapes of the border region. Alongside other environmentalists, I have been documenting the destruction of its habitat Wars are usually measured in the number of people killed, homes destroyed and towns erased. Far less attention is paid to what happens beneath the rubble. Across southern Lebanon, repeated large-scale detonations are not only causing human tragedy by demolishing villages , they are also destroying the ancient limestone habitats that have sheltered colonies of rock hyrax for centuries. As founder and president of Green Southerners, an environmental organisation documenting the ecological effects of war in southern Lebanon, I have been helping colleagues to record the damage inflicted on forests, wildlife and fragile ecosystems across the border region. Continue reading...

data.title: Tommy Robinson: Where’s the Money Gone? review – endless shocking allegations
data.description: From his claim of being ‘de-banked’ to a disturbing detail about a rape survivor’s story being used to fundraise, this film puts big questions to the co-founder of the English Defence League. But it is frustratingly hard to get answers You can’t say it would be a huge surprise if a leading figure of the British far right turned out to be a fraudster: that whole strand of politics is, after all, a con job preying on angry citizens who are daft enough to believe that immigrants, and not the rapaciously greedy super-rich, are somehow the cause of the nation’s problems. If people will fall for that, fleecing them out of their money is not a big leap. Tommy Robinson, co-founder of the English Defence League and now an influencer, independent documentary-maker and international flag-shaggers’ guru, was convicted of mortgage fraud in 2014, but what about 2026? Is he a scam artist juicing idiots for cash? Robinson, real name Stephen Christopher Yaxley-Lennon, is undeniably a talented harvester of donations from his fans, whether it’s in person at his rallies or via the internet: in a video posted online, he admits to “continually ask[ing] you, the people, to support us”, and in another he boasts of having once convinced his admirers to hand over £350,000 in the space of two weeks. If you try to avoid seeing or hearing about Robinson, the amount of money he generates may shock you. Tommy Robinson: Where’s the Money Gone? is on Channel 4 now. Continue reading...

data.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for a not-sachertorte | A kitchen in Rome
data.description: A chocolate cake inspired by the Sacher hotel in Vienna’s trademark creation and emulated by a local Roman pasticceria This column began two years ago, almost to the day, when I made a birthday cake for a friend. “I don’t mind,” was her reply when I first asked what sort of cake she would like. But then, a few minutes later, she said: “Hang on, I mean chocolate with glossy icing. Like the mini ones they make at Barberini .” Barberini is a local bar and cake shop, and the mini cakes she was referring to are their sacher (inspired by sachertorte , of course) – chocolate sponge cakes with a heart of apricot jam and a glossy, chocolate glaze. At Barberini, each one is the size of a single draughts piece, but deep, so not quite two bites but slightly too big for one, unless you open your mouth very wide. “You mean sachertorte?” I said. “That would be great,” was her reply, before changing the subject to I can’t remember what. Walking home, I regretted asking. Continue reading...

data.title: Is Burnham trying to appease Trump? Or Reform? What other reason is there for these North Sea oil plans? | George Monbiot
data.description: Climate catastrophe is on our doorstep – yet Labour’s impending approval of further drilling will bring more pain for negligible gains Pinch yourself, it’s happening again. Here is a Labour government spending a vast amount of political capital to earn tiny material gains while risking huge political losses. It occurred repeatedly under Keir Starmer, and now – with the impending decision to approve further gas and oil drilling in the North Sea – it is happening under Andy Burnham. You rack your brains to explain it, but no rational explanation comes. Burnham is studiously cryptic about his reasons. His clearest statement to date goes as follows: “There is a resource there. When people are struggling, we can’t ignore that.” Does he mean that oil and gas workers are struggling? If so, this decision will be of little use to them. The Jackdaw gasfield, likely to be approved this week, will generate a grand total of 27 direct full-time jobs . The Rosebank oilfield, whose approval is likely to follow soon, will support 450 UK-based jobs during its lifetime. Yet the UK’s net zero economy directly employs 300,000 people , and a further 400,000 jobs are planned. The rest of the green economy employs more than 600,000 . A just transition for fossil fuel workers, securing jobs in the green economy, is better for everyone. George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Seven of my colleagues were killed in Gaza. There and in Ukraine, aid workers are no longer safe | José Andrés
data.description: It now seems the 2024 attack on World Central Kitchen workers was a deliberate IDF tactic. The protections of the Geneva conventions have become paper thin José Andrés is the founder of the food aid charity World Central Kitchen In times of war, the hard and vital work of supplying food, water and medicine has been protected by international agreements for almost 80 years . Yet those protections have been systematically and repeatedly ignored in the two most bloody wars of recent years: Ukraine and Gaza. Russia has attacked healthcare targets in Ukraine more than 3,200 times since the full-scale invasion in February 2022, according to the World Health Organization : about twice a day on average. That includes many “double-tap” attacks on the same target in quick succession, which are especially lethal for first responders. José Andrés is the founder of the food aid charity World Central Kitchen, and a Michelin-starred chef Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Jamaica’s plea to the king: use your authority to ensure colonial slavery is examined | Olivia Grange
data.description: The UK drew immense wealth from our country. But was the slavery that underpinned the empire ever lawful? We deserve a fair hearing Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles On 6 September 1781, the Zong slave ship set out on the final leg of its voyage to Black River, Jamaica. Four hundred and forty two enslaved Africans were on board – twice the number of people the ship could safely accommodate. Twelve weeks later, 132 enslaved people were murdered by the ship’s crew by being pushed overboard to their deaths. The crew’s justification was the ship had insufficient water supplies to keep everyone alive for the rest of the voyage – a claim later proved false in the British courts. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on UK-EU relations: voters would reward greater ambition | Editorial
data.description: The architects of Brexit know it has failed. That presents Andy Burnham with an opportunity to set a bolder new agenda Modesty is not a trait commonly associated with Nigel Farage. Something else must explain the Reform UK leader’s reluctance to talk about what is undoubtedly his biggest achievement. Few individuals can boast of having influenced British politics as drastically as Mr Farage, with his record of campaigning for Brexit before that word was even coined. He will for ever be associated with the demand for emancipation from Brussels, but is rarely heard celebrating its completion. It barely earned a mention in speeches at his party’s annual conference last week. The simple reason is that none of the promises made about the benefits of life outside the EU have been fulfilled. Leaving made the country poorer , and voters know it. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on Donald Trump’s oil deal: Venezuela pays for his vanity | Editorial
data.description: The US president seized a nation’s natural wealth in a modern-day version of gunboat diplomacy to feed his ego – not to lower Americans’ fuel bills Imperialism does not require a flag to be planted or a governor dispatched. It can be a powerful nation deciding who governs a smaller, weaker country, and on what terms and for whose benefit its resources will be developed. Donald Trump’s kidnapping of Venezuela’s Nicolás Maduro, putting his deputy – Delcy Rodríguez – in his place as president, and then her signing a deal handing a fifth of the country’s proven oil reserves to the US , amount to a modern version of 19th-century gunboat diplomacy. Regime change supplied America’s commercial concession. This won’t bother Mr Trump. But it should. The US president has oversold his neocolonial spoils. The additional production Venezuela is supposed to bring online might bring down oil prices eventually, but not anytime soon. Crucially, what Mr Trump calls “t he biggest oil deal in history ” won’t cause the price at the pump to fall before November’s midterms. When so many American voters are struggling to pay energy bills , it’s hard to see how unrealised Orinoco Belt riches are going to help Republican candidates. data.title: ‘That’s how it started’: Dambrauskas’ journey from Who Wants to Be a Millionaire to Champions League
data.description: Valdas Dambrauskas takes Sabah to Manchester United after journeying from Lithuania and a game show win, via London pub work Valdas Dambrauskas can reel off the questions and answers without a moment’s pause. Who won the first Academy Award for best actor in 1929? It was Emil Jannings, even if someone else might have been tempted to go with Charlie Chaplin. Which country publishes the highest number of daily newspapers? India was the clear winner. Can you name the nation that produces the most electricity per capita in the world? His family, watching back home, clasped heads in hands but he was right: back then, in 2002, the answer was his native Lithuania. It was enough to win Dambrauskas about £725 in his appearance on Six Zeros – A Million, the Lithuanian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? “At that time it was quite big money,” he says. “I could have bought a flat in my home town; it was a very difficult period there and they were almost free. data.title: Coco Gauff draws on Tiafoe and ‘delusional’ self-belief in US Open escape
data.description: American rallies from brink to defeat Andreeva Gauff survives 12 double faults in three-set escape Coco Gauff has played far cleaner matches than on Wednesday afternoon. But few players today on the women’s tour have become better at finding answers on the fly when almost nothing is working for them. The 22-year-old American’s serene march through the US Open women’s draw hit extreme turbulence early in her quarter-final clash with fifth-seeded Mirra Andreeva inside Arthur Ashe Stadium. She dropped the first four games before surrendering the opening set in 26 minutes, ending a streak of 20 consecutive sets won dating back nearly a month. She piled up 12 double faults and 42 unforced errors, the majority off a forehand in open revolt. She found herself one point from defeat not once but twice during a hairy second-set tiebreaker. Continue reading...

data.title: Alexis Mac Allister makes his point as Liverpool fight back to defeat Atlético
data.description: It was the time and place for Alexis Mac Allister to do his talking on the pitch and the disgruntled Liverpool midfielder delivered on cue. “Very sad” over Liverpool’s refusal to offer him a new contract, while Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch were getting theirs, Mac Allister made Anfield very happy with a match-winning display against Atlético Madrid. The Argentina international, one of five World Cup finalists involved in an absorbing, delicately-poised contest, vented his frustrations in the best possible and most professional way – from behind an immaculate 20-yard strike into Jan Oblak’s goal rather than a microphone. Mac Allister believes he is playing for a new deal this season and promised to give “100% to my last day” at the pre-match press conference. He was true to his word to extend Atlético’s winless sequence against English opposition in the Champions League league phase to 11 matches. Continue reading...

Perhaps it was the fact that, at Uefa’s insistence, they were forced to wear red shorts for the first time since a Premier League game against Watford in 2022 that Arsenal were not quite at their flowing best here and missed a hatful of chances. data.title: Infantino installs loyalist to oversee Caribbean as he splits Fifa management
data.description: Critics view Fernandes job as move to shore up position Fifa says change is designed to make sport ‘truly global’ Gianni Infantino has separated Fifa’s management of the Caribbean countries from the rest of Concacaf in a move widely regarded by his opponents as an attempt to split the alliance to remove him from office. Concacaf covers North and Central America as well as the Caribbean and was previously managed as one bloc. But the Guardian has learned that the former Switzerland midfielder Gelson Fernandes, an Infantino loyalist, has been appointed as the director of member associations for the Caribbean, in addition to his position looking after Fifa’s African members. Continue reading...

data.title: Can an entire Arctic ecosystem evolve to adapt to the climate crisis?
data.description: In the first project of its kind, scientists are trying to answer if the future of Alaska’s streams and tundra may depend not on survival of the fittest but on how species adapt together On Alaska’s North Slope, scientists tread carefully across clumps of tussock grasses toward a fast-flowing stream draining the imposing Brooks Range of ice and snow. Near Galbraith Creek, they string out a mist net for white-crowned sparrows. The birds have recently arrived from southerly latitudes, intent on feasting on the insects that will soon descend on the tundra like storm clouds. The Arctic summer is short-lived, and sparrows have only a few weeks to establish territories, find mates, lay eggs and raise their chicks on a steady diet of bugs. From every ensnared bird, the scientists collect blood, feather and faecal samples to see what they are eating and how that changes over the summer. Galbraith Creek on Alaska’s North Slope Continue reading...

data.title: Hawaii’s western islands see significant damage as Hurricane Lowell passes by
data.description: Storm didn’t make direct hit but fierce winds downed trees and caused widespread power outages on Kauai Damaging winds and heavy rains from Hurricane Lowell caused significant damage on Hawaii’s western islands, knocking out power to thousands, ripping up stretches of road and drenching homes and stores with mud. Fierce winds downed trees and caused widespread power outages on the island of Kauai, home to 73,000 residents. The Kauai Island Utility Cooperative reported that nearly all of its roughly 35,000 members were without power on Tuesday. About 30,500 customers remained affected by outages as of Wednesday afternoon. Continue reading...

Is there a significant chance of “a Chornobyl-sized catastrophe”. Might there even be a greater than 10% chance that AI could “kill all humans” in the next decade? These warnings were issued over the past 48 hours on both sides of the Atlantic about the potential impact of a technology that most people still think of as a more talkative search engine. data.title: Indonesian foragers may have sucked on mind-altering nuts 25,000 years ago, research finds
data.description: Analysis of two skeletons reveals tooth wear and traces of psychoactive substance in what may be earliest known evidence for human drug taking What may be the earliest known evidence for human drug taking has been traced to ancient Indonesian foragers who sucked on mind-altering nuts as long as 25,000 years ago. Analysis of two exceptionally rare skeletons from the Indonesian island of Sulawesi revealed dramatic tooth wear and traces of a psychoactive substance in the individuals’ remaining teeth, suggesting they routinely sucked on hard, abrasive betel nuts. Continue reading...

data.title: Pressure review – stormy weather in tense D-day forecast retelling
data.description: Andrew Scott finds levels of complexity in a stoic character based on  meteorologist James Stagg, the man who persuaded Eisenhower to delay Operation Overlord, for this slick wartime drama The historic gamble of D-day 1944 gets a new perspective in this slick and watchable, if slightly cheesy and unreflective, period drama, whose staginess reflects its origins in theatre; David Haig adapts his play with the director Anthony Maras. Andrew Scott – in RAF uniform, short-back-and-sides and ’tache – plays James Stagg, a brilliant Scottish meteorologist attached to the military during the war. Stagg arrives at the top-secret allied base of Southwick House in Hampshire stubbornly intent on telling allied Cmdr Dwight “Ike” Eisenhower, bullishly played by Brendan Fraser, that he has an outlier forecast of bad weather, which means D-day should be delayed from Eisenhower’s planned date of 5 June. This is to the rage of Col Irving P Krick (Chris Messina), the swaggeringly gung-ho American meteorologist who has always had Ike’s confidence until now. And if we were unsure about this character’s brash-Yank status, in his opening scene he literally shimmies and bops to the Andrews Sisters’ Boogie-Woogie Bugle Boy in the operations room to the uptight, thin-lipped astonishment of Stagg who, as overall commanding officer, tells the Americans to get that piano out of there. Continue reading...

data.title: The Fire Within You review – overheated family Christmas boils up too many stereotypes
data.description: Venice film festival: Edoardo De Angelis’s claustrophobic drama brings a raging mother up from Naples for the holidays, with a capon. What could possibly not go wrong? If there were a Golden Lion award for the most Italian film in Venice competition it would go to Edoardo De Angelis’s squawking domestic spat of a picture which contains an imperious matriarch, a pained Catholic priest, an argumentative family, and food, so much food. Bowls are stirred and pans are brandished. Pots are seen rattling angrily on the stove. The festival organisers like to deploy a little judicious home cooking when it comes to the selection and De Angelis is already a favoured guest, having opened the 2023 event with his war drama Comandante . But I fear they may have miscalculated with this one. It’s overdone, on the turn and too liberally salted with tears. It’s liable to provoke the occasional stab of heartburn. At the head of the table sits the incorrigible Angela (Vanessa Scalera). She’s up from Naples (where she was presumably once a girl from the backstreets, begging in rags) to supervise Christmas Eve dinner at her son’s book-lined apartment in Milan. Angela’s a relic of the old world, breezily unreconstructed and openly disgusted by the woke state of her grandchildren. “One’s a gay dancer and the other’s a vegetarian,” she scoffs. They in turn are perturbed by the fact that she has brought in a live chicken to be cooked as the main course. Who’s going to catch it? Who’s going to kill it? What even is this creature, exactly? “It’s not a hen, it’s a capon,” sighs middle-aged Anto (Lino Musella), who dearly wishes his mother had never come at all. She’s a beautiful woman, he says, but she smells. Continue reading...

data.title: La Femme Infidèle review – Chabrol’s eerie domestic thriller is a brilliant ballet of repression and fear
data.description: Claude Chabrol’s 1969 film charts a complex marriage in which a husband suspects his wife is cheating on him Writer-director Claude Chabrol’s eerie 1969 masterpiece of frozen emotions and unspoken truths is now rereleased, alongside a Chabrol season at London’s BFI Southbank. This is the suspense thriller remade by Adrian Lyne in 2002 as Unfaithful with Richard Gere and Diane Lane and (partly) remade again this year as Minotaur , a bitter and brilliant theme-variation by the Russian director Andrey Zvyagintsev. As for the original, watched again now, it does not in fact look like a classic noir thriller in the style of Chabrol’s hero Hitchcock, which is how it is often described, but more like something by Buñuel: an elaborate absurdist joke at the expense of the French bourgeoisie, a ballet of repression and fear. The unfaithful woman of the title is the glacially beautiful but glassy-eyed Hélène, played by Chabrol’s then wife Stéphane Audran. She is cheating on Charles, played by Michel Bouquet, her prosperous husband and the father of their adored 10-year-old son. Charles has begun to suspect something is going on during his wife’s frequent trips to Paris, where she supposedly has appointments with the beautician, goes shopping or visits the cinema, but in fact has sex with the divorced writer Victor Pegala (Maurice Ronet) at his dishevelled bachelor flat. Charles phones the beauty parlour where she is supposed to be getting a treatment; she isn’t there. We see how this only confirms suspicions which have clearly accumulated in his mind like silt over months or even years. Continue reading...

data.title: Inglourious baristas: why is Brad Pitt making coffee for 16 abusive dogs?
data.description: In new film The Heart of the Beast, the A-lister’s bond with his loyal mutt proves crucial. In Spike Jonze’s new advert, Pitt is rather more subservient Brad Pitt has a new movie out this month, The Heart of the Beast, about an emotionally damaged man who forms a life-saving bond with a dog. If that sounds familiar, maybe it is because you have seen The Call of the Wild. Or maybe it is because you have seen A Dog’s Way Home. Or maybe it is because you have seen Dog. Or, look, you get the idea. But perhaps Brad Pitt knows that getting people to see something as unimaginative as The Heart of the Beast is an uphill struggle, because that would explain why he has just made an advert that looks and feels much more like the Brad Pitt dog movie that deserves to be made. In short, it is an advert where Brad Pitt gets loudly disparaged by a number of dogs for an extended period of time. Continue reading...

data.title: Call My Agent! The Movie review – the gang get back together and c’est formidable
data.description: The screwball French comedy is back as a film that actually works, thanks to putting Andréa and Noémie at the heart of chaotic events and bringing all the old faces back At last: a beloved-TV-show-to-film-spinoff that doesn’t suck! The original French series is a screwball-speed office comedy about a boutique Parisian talent agency, and was a ratings and critical success in its homeland when it started back in 2015. Its acquisition by Netflix grew the audience internationally and spawned a stable full of remakes across Europe and Asia. In the meantime, several members of the original French cast have become proper stars in their own right, especially Camille Cottin and Laure Calamy, and this sequel, set five years on, is smart to put these two at the heart of the latest instalment. And of course, there are the obligatory turns from properly famous actors playing themselves, including Laetitia Casta, Vincent Macaigne, Laurent Lafitte and some guy named George Clooney, best known these days for appearances on vaporettos in the Venice lagoon. Like many great sitcoms, this one always understood that failure, rather than success, keeps the wider narrative arc more interesting and relatable. So the last episode of the series left the gang at talent agency ASK (which stood for Agence Samuel Kerr, after the founder, who died in the first episode), dispersed to new gigs and careers; the band, in effect, broke up. Five years on, the stars have aligned to bring them all back together to work on Andréa (Cottin) and Noémie’s (Calamy) new film project, so the title Call My Agent! The Movie works on more than one level. Continue reading...

data.title: Union Town review – passionate exposé of US delivery workers’ employment conditions
data.description: Venice film festival: Barbara Kopple returns with her third film investigating US workers’ rights – this time, undocumented ‘deliveristas’ and the attempts to unionise Amazon staff Barbara Kopple’s documentary about app-based delivery workers is a stirring, defiant, battle-hardened affair, swinging between the fraught picket line and the still more hazardous New York City streets. It’s a new film that feels old in the best sense of the word; a hoarse battle cry that summons the ghosts of The Grapes of Wrath and the New Deal, Eugene Debs and Woody Guthrie. That America is long dead and buried, a casualty of changing times, but Kopple sees no reason why it should not rise again. Union Town, tellingly, is the third part of a loose trilogy which serves as an ongoing audit of US workers’ rights. This began with 1976’s Harlan County, USA, which tackled a Kentucky miners’ strike, and continued through 1990’s American Dream, which covered a meatpacking plant in Austin, Minnesota. Since then, however, the culture has shifted, atomised, with the big corporations increasingly reliant on a shadow economy of undocumented workers. Kopple’s “deliveristas” ferry packages for the likes of Amazon and DoorDash but they are technically third-party contractors. That means if, say, they happen to be injured in the line of duty, they cover the hospital bills and repairs to the bike. It also means that they are likely to be fired while they’re laid up in bed. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It detonated right outside our house’: the explosion that started an incredible podcast series
data.description: Josh Baker is the journalist behind the BBC’s smash hit I’m Not a Monster. He’s back with his most extraordinary investigation yet – to solve the mystery of Austin Tice, who disappeared in Syria 14 years ago In 2012, the US marine turned freelance foreign correspondent Austin Tice disappeared in Syria. If he’s still alive, he’ll be the second-longest detained journalist in the world. That, says Josh Baker (speaking to me from Wales), was the podcast he thought he was making: “We thought we were looking for a missing person, and what we fell into was almost like a Bourne novel, utterly extraordinary. A world of espionage, spies, dictatorship.” It’s also a story of American exceptionalism – the way the US saw itself in relation to the rest of the world. Moreover, “I don’t mean this in a crass way,” Baker says, “but through Austin’s story, we also learn a lot about the last 14 years of the civil war in Syria. We really go inside the regime’s industrial complex of disappearance and torture. As episode two begins, Assad is gone, and we enter into these facilities.” Continue reading...

data.title: Even better than the Real Thing? The overlooked Black music scene of 1970s Liverpool
data.description: Despite the city’s backdrop of deprivation and racism, vibrant nightclubs and daring artists thrived – but after No 1 success for the Real Thing, why was the scene ignored? Months before the Real Thing’s You to Me Are Everything became a UK No 1 hit in 1976, lead singer Chris Amoo took the unreleased song to the Timepiece, a nightclub devoted to Black music tucked in between bars on Liverpool’s Fleet Street. His DJ friend Les Spaine stuck it on, and the empty dancefloor “just filled up, and nobody, not one person in that place, had heard the song before”, Amoo says with pride on a call from his home on the outskirts of Liverpool. “That’s when me and Les looked at each other and thought: you’ve got something there, brother.” The track’s symphonic majesty and romantic vocals captured the hearts of millions, and it peaked in the charts during 1976’s summer heatwave. Fifty years later, Amoo is on tour with his fellow bandmate Dave Smith in celebration of its anniversary. But the Real Thing were just the most high-profile group from an underground funk and R&B scene which emerged in 1970s Liverpool, upheld by a generation, predominately from the Toxteth area south of the city centre, that embraced Black American culture. Continue reading...

data.title: Streaming from the cloud was meant to change games forever – what happened?
data.description: Once hailed as the future, even the likes of Google, Sony and Microsoft have struggled to make streaming games fun, fast or affordable • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here In August 2009, at the very first Gamescom expo, I sat in a small meeting room in Germany and played Mario Kart and World of Warcraft on a laptop, via technology that was then completely new: cloud gaming. It was a demonstration for a yet-to-be-launched service called Gaikai that promised to let you play any game in a browser window, without a console. (Here is an ancient video of that demonstration, featuring a very young Keza.) With a single click I could launch into any game, hosted on servers hundreds of miles away. It really did look like the future. Since then, plenty of companies have tried to be the first to truly crack game streaming, vying to be the Netflix of games. Sony ended up buying Gaikai for $380m (£242m) in 2012; its technology now powers the streamable classic games library on PlayStation, and the PS5’s advanced game streaming. OnLive, Gaikai’s first competitor, launched in 2011 but shut down after less than a year, leaving Sony to acquire all its patents. Google’s Stadia cloud gaming service also imploded, launching in 2019 and shutting down three years later. Continue reading...

data.title: John Malkovich cancels Israel trip over fabricated solidarity quote
data.description: The Wild Horse Nine actor had been due to appear on stage in The Music Critic in Tel Aviv – but pulled out over PR firm’s ‘unacceptable and untenable’ attribution of statement John Malkovich has cancelled a planned trip to Israel next year to appear on stage after a PR firm hired by the show attributed quotes to the actor that the company had written. Malkovich, who is a leading Oscar contender for his role in Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine , was due to appear in The Music Critic, a theatrical-musical satire composed by the Jewish violinist Aleksey Igudesman, in Tel Aviv’s Charles Bronfman Auditorium on 13 April. data.title: Forget vinyl v digital debates, this kind of musical ‘authenticity’ brings real rewards
data.description: Period instruments are miles away from retro affectation, and as two Proms this week will show, can actually bring historical music up to the moment Nostalgia. What a kick. And what a commercial boon for the music industry. Love the sound of 60s pop and 70s disco? You need the original synths if you’re a composer or producer. You listen to music on digital streams? Loser! Join the retro-future of vinyl enthusiasm, and feel the grooves under your fingers like your parents or grandparents used to. Or you can even make music physical again through the horrible medium of cassettes: all that plastic, all those tiny liner notes, all that high-speed dubbing. Retro-futurists cherish what they claim is the extra warmth and sonic richness of vinyl, but there is no acoustic reason why vinyl is better. It is in fact objectively worse as a carrier of sonic information than any high-resolution stream of the same track, song or symphony. For cassette nostalgists, if it’s got that old-fashioned tape hiss, it sounds more “real”. We’re now looking for things to sound less clean. Because we distrust today’s technological utopia, we want signs that our music is less polished, less perfect, and thus more human. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Who do you really believe?’: the true crime fans who became a part of the story
data.description: In HBO’s gripping new docuseries A Killer Story, a crusading couple become convinced that woman accused of murder is innocent A man and a woman are murdered in cold blood inside their Topeka, Kansas, bedroom under cover of darkness in 2002. Suspicion quickly falls on the man’s ex-wife, Dana Chandler, with family and forensic evidence painting her as the jealous type. But the county prosecutor at the time declines to pursue charges in large part because nothing places Chandler at the scene of the crime. It’s only after a politically motivated prosecutor is appointed and CBS’s 48 Hours airs a 2009 report rehashing the case that Chandler is arrested on two counts of premeditated first-degree murder in 2011 and condemned to consecutive life sentences the following year. No doubt: the story is hot copy. And more than likely, Chandler’s conviction marks the conclusion if a husband-and-wife team of true crime enthusiasts hadn’t become convinced that the real killer was still walking free. “There’s a lot of questions that remain,” says film-maker Matthew Galkin. “But when you start to unpack the crime itself, there’s a lot of hoops to jump through and a very high bar to clear in order for her to have pulled this off.” Continue reading...

data.title: Péter Nádas obituary
data.description: Hungarian author who explored memory and history in his fiction and was nominated for a Nobel prize The writer Péter Nádas, who has died aged 83, transformed the modern history of his native Hungary into epic fiction that rooted its upheavals and calamities in the minds, and bodies, of his all-too-human characters. “I’m not a historian,” he said. “I’m not an anthropologist, nor am I a sociologist. I work with the fates of individuals.” Those individuals filled a series of books that, in their scope, depth and stylistic ambition, made Nádas a perennial contender for the Nobel prize in literature. Yet it would be his younger compatriot László Krasznahorkai, drawing on the senior writer’s example, who took that honour in 2025 . Continue reading...

data.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: this sweltering summer, I finally stopped giving a tuck
data.description: I’ve always cinched my outfits at the waist, but shifting to a looser silhouette has helped me keep my cool in more ways than one This was the summer of the Great Untuck. The long hot summer of 2026 finally taught me to do what fashion has been nagging me about for years, which is to quit tucking in my shirts and T-shirts. To stop assuming that the top half of an outfit must be neatly cinched by the waistband of the skirt or trousers. It wasn’t a style epiphany, to be fair. It was just too hot to do anything else. An extended run of hot weather at home changes how you dress. In the old-school type of British heatwave, which lasted about half a week, I was too giddy with excitement at not having to wear a cardigan to think more strategically. But this summer was different. And eventually I discovered what hot-climate cultures have always known, which is that loose, generously sized clothing that maximises sun protection while minimising skin contact is way more pleasant to wear in the heat than anything short and tight. Continue reading...

data.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: the hero products that kept me cool in the long hot summer of 2026
data.description: From face tints and self-tan to summer scents, these lightweight buys saw me through multiple heatwaves You’ll normally find me looking back on my favourite products of the past 12 months at year’s end. But this summer has been so freakishly hot and sweaty it has required its own toolkit and, by extension, its own list of exceptionally well-performing products that deserve rapturous commendation. The first is Refy’s Skin Base (£30), a sheer face tint so thin and so lightweight it has been all I could bear to wear since July. It’s suitable for all skin types, but not at all appropriate for those who hate any hint of shine. While the texture is totally ungreasy, breathable and so comfortable as to be imperceptible, it does look unmistakably dewy, so avoid if you’re devoted to matte. Personally, I take the view that, in this heat, one might as well steer into the skid, but I am, admittedly, at an age when a juicier look works in my skin’s favour. Anyway, this is makeup that truly feels like absolutely nothing, and what it lacks in coverage can be made up with concealer where needed. Maximum points from me (I wear shade 140N). Continue reading...

data.title: ‘How do we make time for intimacy?’: sex expert Alix Fox answered your questions
data.description: Sexual culture and wellbeing expert Alix Fox answered your questions about how to have a healthier, happier, hornier love life Greygoose77 asks : Can electronic sex toys cause desensitisation? Alix: Short answer: nope. But they can temporarily alter the threshold of stimulatory intensity that you require in order to get off. That has been covered more fully here . Alix: Mate, I hear you. And I suspect you’re going to sigh with all the power of a wind tunnel when I tell you that unless you prioritise intimacy, it isn’t going to happen. You have to block in time for it – which will likely mean booting something else out of your diary. That can seem hard at first, when EVERYTHING feels important if not essential. But what’s harder is mourning a dwindling love life. Plus, having a sexy, silly, scrumptious time with a lover can be like a triple espresso when it comes to putting a pep in your step and soothing everyday stress. It may sound trite, but when intimacy functions as a therapeutic release, ‘doing it’ can actually help you get other things done. To be clear, I’m talking about scheduling intimacy, not necessarily intercourse . Nobody should feel duty bound to engage in any particular physical act when the allotted date rolls round. You may find it helpful (and a welcome turn on) to write a ‘menu’ of different erotic ‘dishes’ you might like to choose from during a date night, ranging from more delicate flavours like having your hair washed for you or a bubble bath for two, to spicier exploits like taking turns to read from an explicit book. Dr Sara Nasserzadeh, author of Love by Design: 6 Ingredients to Build a Lifetime of Love , says “scheduled sexy time should feel like a restaurant reservation: sometimes you’ll fancy a lighter meal; other times, a richer dish. You may both pick different courses, or feel drawn to the same plate. The only criteria is that everyone comes away satisfied – which doesn’t always require orgasm, by the way.” Continue reading...

data.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: can playing a video game count as cheating on your partner?
data.description: Historically a new Grand Theft Auto game inspired controversy around violence – but this time people are getting exercised about its romance There was never any doubt that Grand Theft Auto VI’s extended look would elicit a viral reaction from the internet. Having won the Game Awards’ Most Anticipated award twice consecutively, Rockstar’s forthcoming crime opus is one of the most frothed-over games in recent memory, or indeed ever. It’s nothing short of a cultural phenomenon . One aspect of the game has provoked an unexpectedly vehement response on social media: not violence, but romance. Protagonists Lucia and Jason are in love, you see, and as a player, part of your job is keeping their spark alive and their relationship strong, so that their criminal escapades are underpinned by a strong connection to one another. Holding hands, enjoying a date at the beach, spontaneously texting one another when apart – all of these interactions will strengthen their bond. You’ll be putting in a lot of work to ensure this couple thrives, which is why some people have come to believe that playing GTA VI counts as micro-cheating. Continue reading...

data.title: In 2017, USGS released 72.57 kg of dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River; aircraft tracked it from above
data.description: In 2017, the US Geological Survey released 72.57 kg of Rhodamine WT dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River over 90 seconds to study how a tracer moves through flowing water. Researchers tracked the dye using instruments in the river and hyperspectral images captured from an aircraft flying 1,000 metres above the ground, with images recorded in 0.5-metre pixels across 48 spectral bands.

data.title: Gateshead uses 150m-deep mine water to heat 350 homes and public buildings
data.description: Water from deep beneath Gateshead now heats hundreds of homes and buildings. A six-megawatt heat pump extracts warmth from mine water, feeding a district network. This system, the largest of its kind in Great Britain, became operational in March 2023. Over five kilometers of pipes distribute the heated water to various public and private properties. Researchers are studying the mine water system through the Gateshead Living Laboratory.

data.title: Scientists discover apple waste can remove up to 100% of lead from water
data.description: Researchers explored apple pomace for removing lead ions from contaminated water. Both raw and processed apple waste effectively removed lead from the solution. Extracted apple waste achieved complete lead removal under optimal experimental conditions. The biosorbents demonstrated rapid lead adsorption within the first hour of testing. These findings highlight apple pomace's potential for environmental remediation applications.

Its preservation highlights the journey of renewable energy progress in Australia and serves as a symbol of the nation's aspirations for a sustainable energy future.

data.title: Britain’s vulnerable sharks to be tracked with 70 tags and catch records since 1953
data.description: A new three-year research initiative is set to study three at-risk shark species in British waters. By using electronic tags to monitor their movements and diving behaviors, the team will analyze historical distribution data from anglers spanning decades. This comprehensive approach aims to enhance understanding of shark migration and behavior, ultimately contributing to effective conservation efforts for these essential marine creatures.

data.title: Canada released 26 bison into Banff in 2017; 9 years later, the herd has grown rapidly
data.description: Parks Canada successfully reintroduced plains bison into Banff National Park starting in 2017. The population grew from sixteen animals to about eighty by autumn 2022.  Monitoring showed bison adapted to mountain habitat, preferring higher elevations for forage.  Natural mortality remained low, with only two deaths recorded during the pilot.  The five-year program achieved a 33% average annual population growth rate.

Les habitants s’inquiètent, le maire rachète les terres, les agriculteurs se sentent stigmatisés, et la zone industrio-portuaire de La Rochelle est montrée du doigt.

data.title: Août 2026 est le mois le plus chaud jamais mesuré dans le monde, Copernicus alerte sur des risques accrus pour l’Europe

data.title: Narcisismo conversacional transforma diálogo em monólogo
data.description: Certas pessoas são capazes de sequestrar a conversa mais trágica, aleatória ou íntima para contar uma história pessoal ou registrar sua opinião. Isso tem até nome: narcisismo conversacional. O conceito é bem mais antigo do que as redes sociais fazem parecer. No livro "The Pursuit of Attention" (A Busca Pela Atenção, em tradução), de 1979, o sociólogo norte-americano Charles Derber descreveu esse tipo de comportamento. Na época, a internet ainda era só um projeto militar e a atenção estava longe de ser um recurso tão valioso e escasso. Leia mais (09/10/2026 - 04h00)

data.title: Parque das Águas é a estrela de São Lourenço, no sul de Minas
data.description: Não é à toa que a cidade de São Lourenço integra o chamado circuito das águas de Minas Gerais . Sua principal estrela, visita obrigatória para os turistas, é o quase centenário Parque das Águas. Fundado em 1936, o parque possui 430 mil metros quadrados de Mata Atlântica preservada e nove fontes de águas minerais, com composição físico-química e características distintas. Em cada uma delas, há placas com essas informações e a quais terapias de saúde as águas estão associadas. Ao caminhar pelas alamedas do parque, à sombra das árvores, o visitante se depara com as fontes, mas elas não são a única atração. Há aluguel de bicicletas, quadras esportivas, pista de caminhada, área para pescaria, bocha e patinação. Na hora da pausa, o visitante pode escolher entre um restaurante e um café, que serve affogatos e outras bebidas com cafés produzidos na região. Leia mais (09/09/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Andradas conquista com vinícolas, hospitalidade e natureza da Mantiqueira
data.description: Aos pés da serra da Mantiqueira, Andradas (MG) encanta pelo ar de interior e por suas atrações naturais e vinícolas. Faz divisa com São Paulo, mas quando se chega lá, ao ouvir o sotaque mineirinho dos moradores, não há dúvidas de que estamos em Minas Gerais . Aí é só aproveitar a hospitalidade mineira, que tem se profissionalizado ano a ano. Na última década, a cidade viveu um boom no turismo, com a inauguração de dois novos hotéis, abertura de chalés e maior oferta de passeios nas vinícolas. Uma delas é a Casa Geraldo, que em junho conquistou duas medalhas no prêmio Decanter World Wine Awards , um dos mais importantes do setor no mundo. Além da produção de vinhos, iniciada em 1969 por descendentes de italianos, a empresa possui um complexo para receber visitantes, com um restaurante e opções de passeios. Neles, os enófilos visitam os parreirais e experimentam os produtos da casa. Leia mais (09/09/2026 - 22h58)

data.title: Trilhos de trem marcam paisagem de Passa Quatro, no sul de Minas
data.description: A estrada de ferro se impõe na paisagem de Passa Quatro mesmo antes de chegarmos a esta cidade do sul de Minas Gerais . E quando se está lá, não há como ignorá-la: seus trilhos cortam o município de ponta a ponta. Por ela corre, aos finais de semana e feriados, o Trem da Serra da Mantiqueira, em trajeto de 20 km entre as estações de Passa Quatro e Coronel Fulgêncio. Em uma locomotiva, o passeio de duas horas reconstitui um pequeno trecho da estrada de ferro Minas/Rio, inaugurada em 1884 com a presença de Dom Pedro 2º. Durante o percurso, um violeiro anima o público, e a natureza da serra da Mantiqueira, vista pelas janelas, encanta a todos. Ao chegar à estação Coronel Fulgêncio, os turistas caminham até o Túnel da Mantiqueira, passagem ferroviária com cerca de 900 metros na divisa de São Paulo com Minas. Leia mais (09/09/2026 - 22h57)

data.title: Caldas, no sul de Minas, encanta pelas águas e pela natureza
data.description: A natureza esculpida há milhões de anos guia a visita à cidade de Caldas, no sul de Minas Gerais . Fundado em território de origem vulcânica, o município é repleto de pedras, montanhas da Mantiqueira e cachoeiras e tem em suas fontes de águas sulfurosas uma de suas principais atrações. E são justamente essas águas que unem essa história dos primórdios a outra mais recente. Segundo a prefeitura da cidade, as propriedades medicinais de fontes do distrito de Pocinhos do Rio Verde já eram conhecidas desde ao menos 1850. Em 1910, começou sua exploração comercial, a partir da criação de um balneário. Com o passar dos anos, empresas se sucederam na administração do empreendimento, até que fosse transferido para a administração municipal. Atualmente, o Balneário Reynaldo de Oliveira Pimenta, localizado às margens do rio Verde, oferece banhos, sauna, massagens e tratamentos com águas sulfurosas e radioativas que vêm de três fontes locais. Os preços variam de R$ 30 (banho de imersão por 20 minutos) a R$ 200 (pacote de dez banhos). É possível alugar roupões e toalhas. Leia mais (09/09/2026 - 22h56)

data.title: Fachin reage, tira poder de Moraes e fica a dúvida sobre a tentativa de criar Xandão da extrema direita
data.description: Edson Fachin reagiu, nos acréscimos. Suspendeu a partida por causa de pancadaria generalizada, como diz o clichê do futebol . Como o jogo vai prosseguir, se com mais intervenção da polícia (de Fachin), se a partida vai para os pênaltis ou até para o tiroteio, não se sabe. Mas o presidente do Supremo reagiu ao fato de que ministros se digladiavam publicamente com decisões que ameaçam a ordem mais básica (qual lei ou decisão vale?) e o atropelavam até em casos que estavam na mão dele, de Fachin. "Delineia-se, assim, quadro de conflitos e sobreposições processuais que configuram grave lesão à ordem pública", escreveu o presidente do STF . Leia mais (09/09/2026 - 20h40)

data.description: Den långsiktiga drömmen om en OS-medalj ska nås en hundradel i taget. Redan nu kan han dock titulera sig ”en av de bästa i världen” som deltagare i Ultimate Championship. – Det kommer ju vara jätteballt att gå runt bland de absolut bästa i varje gren. Men det är där man vill höra hemma, säger häcklöparen Oskar Edlund – som tror att en förklaring till årets lyft stavas havregrynsgröt.

data.title: Efter fyra år med Tidö – det här efterfrågar Kultursverige

data.title: Kommer bråken stoppa en Andersson-regering?
data.description: Dramatiken ökar inför valdagen, men alltjämt tycks oppositionen leda i mätningarna. Om Magdalena Andersson får bilda regering, hur ska det fungera tillsammans med två partier som bråkar så mycket med varandra? Vänsterpartiet kräver att för första gången få plats i en regering – Centerpartiet säger att de hellre går till extraval än tillåter just det. Är det verkligen en klok strategi att försöka formera sig först efter valdagen? Programledare: Måns Mosesson. Med Hans Rosén, politikreporter på DN.

data.title: Nowy impuls rozwojowy dla Kielc i regionu
data.description: Kielce mogą zyskać obszar inwestycyjny o powierzchni kilkuset hektarów oraz kolejowy terminal towarowy Podczas MSPO w Kielcach podpisane zostały dwa listy intencyjne dotyczące przyszłości terenów w Obicach - z Agencją Rozwoju Przemysłu i Specjalną Strefą Ekonomiczną Starachowice oraz z Centralnym Portem Komunikacyjnym. - Przez wiele lat Obice kojarzyły się przede wszystkim z projektem lotniska. My chcemy spojrzeć na ten teren na nowo i wykorzystać jego ogromny potencjał gospodarczy. Mówimy kilkuset hektarach, które mogą stać się przestrzenią dla dużych inwestycji, nowych technologii i nowych miejsc pracy. Do tego potrzebujemy jednak nie tylko terenów, ale również profesjonalnych partnerów, infrastruktury i dobrego skomunikowania - mówi Agata Wojda, prezydentka Kielc.

data.title: Krótsze postępowania, mediacje i większa ochrona. MEN chce zmienić zasady odpowiedzialności nauczycieli

data.title: Artur Bartkiewicz: W aferze Zondacrypto PiS ma krwawić w kręgu podejrzeń
data.description: Polityczny serial pod roboczym tytułem „Przemysław Kral, Zondacrypto i polska prawica” raczej nie doczeka się odcinka o komisji śledczej. Taka komisja dałaby bowiem PiS jakąś szansę wpłynięcia na agendę związaną z tą sprawą. Dopóki sprawą zajmuje się wyłącznie prokuratura, PiS może działać tylko reaktywnie i wykrwawiać się wraz z kolejnymi odsłonami afery.

data.title: Městský soud v Praze zrušil osvobozující rozsudek v kauze exposlance Feriho
data.description: Městský soud v Praze podle České televize (ČT) zrušil osvobozující rozsudek v kauze bývalého poslance Dominika Feriho, který čelí obžalobě ze znásilnění tehdy sedmnáctileté dívky. data.title: Filozofická fakulta plánuje velké změny, studenti vyjdou na protestní pochod
data.description: Studenti Filozofické fakulty Univerzity Karlovy (FF UK) plánují protestní pochod proti chystaným změnám, které se mají dotknout desítek oborů. Vadí jim také nejasná a netransparentní komunikace vedení a rychlé tempo změn. Pochod vyjde ve 12:15 od pražského Karolina a zamíří k budově filozofické fakulty. Odpoledne se pak má setkat také Akademický senát FF UK, aby reorganizaci projednal.

data.title: Kdy začít čistit zuby dětem? Není potřeba čekat, radí expertka
data.description: Jedna pasta na všechny problémy? Tak jednoduché to není. Jiné složení může být vhodné pro citlivé zuby, jiné při potížích s dásněmi nebo oslabenou sklovinou. Iwona Przybylska ze společnosti Haleon vysvětluje, co zubní pasta opravdu dokáže, kde jsou její limity a jakých chyb se při každodenní péči o zuby vyvarovat.

data.title: Badatelka: Stojím si za tím, že Jan Masaryk byl zavražděn, za nitky tahal Kreml
data.description: Badatelka a spisovatelka Václava Jandečková je přesvědčena, že Jan Masaryk v březnu 1948 nespáchal sebevraždu, ale stal se obětí násilného trestného činu, za nímž mohl stát Sovětský svaz. V Rozstřelu na iDNES.cz popsala svědectví o podivném zranění za jeho uchem i svou verzi toho, jak mohlo být tělo ministra zahraničí dopraveno z okna. Definitivní odpověď by podle ní mohla přinést nedávná exhumace a hlavně nový expertní tým, kterému na rozdíl od předchozích vyšetřovatelů důvěřuje.

data.title: Trumpův let se opozdil. Na jeho novém speciálu se omylem nafoukla skluzavka
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump ve středu odletěl na sjezd své Republikánské strany v Dallasu s mírným zpožděním. Na speciálu Air Force One se totiž nedopatřením nafoukla skluzavka pro evakuaci cestujících v případě nouze. Trump v té době ještě na palubě letounu darovaného Katarem nebyl. Na letištní ploše Andrewsovy základny nedaleko Washingtonu pak vysvětloval, že šlo jen o kontrolu skluzavky, která zabere asi 15 minut.

data.title: Věže spadly a Trump se chlubil. Už jsme neteční k nesvobodě, míní expert o 11. září
data.description: Od zřícení Dvojčat sice uplynulo čtvrt století, důsledky globální války proti terorismu ale zažíváme každý den. „Státem narušené soukromí se stalo naprostou normou,“ říká v rozhovoru pro iDNES Premium analytik Kevin Schwartz z Orientálního ústavu Akademie věd. Mimo jiné popisuje, jak únava z „nekonečných konfliktů“ stvořila Donalda Trumpa. Slovo terorista se podle něj stalo nadužívanou nálepkou.

data.title: Z továrny jsou lofty, z kanceláří byty. Jak Praha dává starým domům druhou šanci?
data.description:
Chátrající činžovní dům, opuštěná továrna nebo dávno nepotřebná telefonní ústředna nemusí skončit demolicí. Staré pražské budovy dostávají nový život, ale jejich proměna 
často naráží na technický stav, památkáře, sousedy i složité povolování. Co rozhoduje o tom, zda se rekonstrukce ještě vyplatí, jak se určuje potenciál a cena činžovního domu a co řeší majitelé, když zvažují prodej nemovitosti či činžovního domu v Praze investorovi?

data.title: Brněnské solární fiasko. Obří projekt se smrskl, z 650 voltaik jich funguje devět
data.description: Byl to ambiciózní plán: Brno založí firmu, která vybuduje na střechách městských budov na 650 fotovoltaických elektráren za 1,5 miliardy korun, a Brno díky tomu ušetří. Projekt, který tlačil hlavně tehdejší náměstek primátorky Brna, exministr životního prostředí Petr Hladík, ale nevyšel. Dnes je v provozu jen devět elektráren, městská firma Sako Brno Solar řeší dluhy, ztráty i vlastní budoucnost.

data.title: Srpen byl celosvětově nejteplejším měsícem historie, informuje Copernicus
data.description: Letošní srpen byl celosvětově nejteplejším měsícem historie, když vyrovnal rekord července 2023. Průměrná teplota vzduchu u zemského povrchu činila 16,96 stupně Celsia a byla o 0,85 stupně nad průměrem z let 1991 až 2020, uvedla služba Evropské unie pro sledování klimatu Copernicus. Letní období od června do srpna vyrovnalo rekord průměrné celosvětové teploty z roku 2024.

data.title: 5000 dolarů všem, kdo zvolí republikány, jinak USA čeká peklo, slibuje a hrozí Trump
data.description: Pokud republikáni po listopadových volbách ztratí v Kongresu většinu, bude to pro Spojené státy znamenat peklo, varoval americký prezident Donald Trump na celonárodním sjezdu své strany v Dallasu. Trump slíbil, že pokud republikáni vyhrají, vyplatí každému dospělému Američanovi 5 tisíc dolarů (skoro 104 300 korun).

data.description: Ve čtvrtek se v Česku ochladí, jen na jihu Moravy může být nepatrně tepleji. Pršet bude jen výjimečně. V pátek se ovšem přeháňky vyskytnou zejména v jihovýchodní části země. data.title: Rusko se snaží paralyzovat Kyjev. Válka bude i v roce 2027, smiřují se USA a Evropa
data.description: Prostě jdete spát a přemýšlíte, jestli se vzbudíte nebo ne. Takový je teď život v Kyjevě, popsala médiím Kyjevanka Darja Kolisnyková. Klid, kterého se ukrajinská metropole po několikadenním ostřelování během víkendové návštěvy amerických vyjednavačů dočkala, je u konce. A zatímco Rusko znovu ostřeluje Ukrajinu a Washington mluví pozitivně o novém kole mírových jednání, USA a Evropa se chystají na válku i v roce 2027.

data.title: Práci přes aplikace čekají nová pravidla. Spor je na tom, kdo je zaměstnanec

data.title: Rita Blanco e Ruben Alves na Grande Entrevista. Perda da identidade de Lisboa "já é uma realidade" mas "não é inevitabilidade"
data.description: É um dos traços da identidade de Lisboa: os casamentos de Santo António mobilizam por alturas de junho casais que escolhem dar o nó com a bênção do Santo padroeiro de Lisboa. Foi a partir desta tradição que o realizador Rúben Alves decidiu criar o seu novo filme, "Santo António, o Casamenteiro de Lisboa", que estreia por estes dias nas salas de cinema de todo o país e conta com a atriz Rita Blanco.

data.title: US backs Lebanese Army in upholding national sovereignty
data.description: DUBAI: The US embassy in Lebanon said on Thursday it supported the Lebanese government in asserting sovereignty and its enforcement by the country’s army. Posting on X, the embassy said it supported ensuring decisions regarding war and peace remained exclusively in the hands of the state. “Every day, the Lebanese people make it clear they prefer Lebanese state institutions over Hezbollah’s weapons. Southern Lebanon does not belong to regional actors or militias,” it said.

data.title: Filosofía peruana hoy: autoconocimiento y libertad
data.description: La reciente publicación de Autoconocimiento y libertad consolida la fecunda trayectoria académica del profesor Pablo Quintanilla en el Perú. En esta obra, el filósofo articula con rigor el vínculo indisociable entre la comprensión reflexiva del propio psiquismo y el ensanchamiento del libre albedrío. Mediante un diálogo fecundo entre análisis conceptual y ciencias cognitivas, el volumen ofrece una lúcida contribución humanista sobre nuestra capacidad para deliberar, convivir y realizarnos.

data.title: L’Assemblée nationale et ONU-Habitat s’accordent pour sauver les villes camerounaises
data.description: © AN Au lendemain du lancement du Plan national villes intelligentes, le partenariat se renforce au sommet. Ce 9 septembre 2026, le président de l'Assemblée nationale, Théodore Datouo, a reçu à Yaoundé Mme Anacláudia Rossbach, sous-secrétaire générale des Nations Unies et directrice exécutive d'ONU-Habitat. Une audience qui s'est tenue en présence de la ministre de l'Habitat et du Développement urbain, Célestine Ketcha Courtès. Si l'ensemble du Cameroun est concerné, c'est la capitale qui a cristallisé les échanges. La patronne d'ONU-Habitat a pointé du doigt les conséquences directes de l'étalement urbain anarchique de Yaoundé sur l'environnement, le climat, les populations et l'activité économique. Elle a abouti au diagnostic selon lequel sans une meilleure planification foncière et territoriale, la ville va continuer à s'étendre au détriment de tout. Elle a plaidé pour une urbanisation maîtrisée et inclusive. Pour accompagner la dynamique, ONU-Habitat a mis sur la table trois leviers. Il s’agit de la décentralisation pour donner plus de pouvoir aux mairies ; de la localisation des ODD pour adapter les objectifs du développement durable aux réalités de chaque ville ; la promotion et la valorisation des matériaux locaux pour construire. Elle a surtout insisté sur un point : il faut une collaboration étroite entre le parlement et le gouvernement pour créer des lois adaptées. De son côté, le président de l'Assemblée nationale a assuré que le Cameroun a "des bases solides" pour renforcer ce partenariat avec l'ONU. Il a mis en avant deux priorités pour le parlement : faciliter l'accès des femmes au logement et à la propriété foncière, présenté comme un levier essentiel d'autonomisation ; accompagner par des lois les efforts pour une urbanisation mieux planifiée. Après l'Exécutif hier avec le lancement du Plan villes intelligentes, c'est désormais le Législatif qui s'engage à créer le cadre juridique pour que ce plan ne reste pas lettre morte. Cet article L’Assemblée nationale et ONU-Habitat s’accordent pour sauver les villes camerounaises est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Tourisme : l’Égypte veut investir au Cameroun
data.description: © DR Reçue le 09 septembre 2026 par le ministre Gabriel Mbairobe, une délégation égyptienne conduite par le ministre Karim Sharif a proposé quatre axes de collaboration : construction d'infrastructures d'hébergement, création de centres de loisirs, formation du personnel hôtelier et échange d'expériences en gestion et tourisme culturel. Le tourisme camerounais attire l'Égypte. Une délégation de haut vol conduite par Karim Sharif, ministre adjoint des Affaires étrangères chargé des Affaires africaines, a été reçue le 09 septembre 2026 au ministère du Tourisme et des Loisirs. Accompagné du Dr Mohamed Mostafa Gad, conseiller du ministre de la Santé, et du général de division Sherif Zakaria, directeur adjoint des transports maritimes, l'émissaire du Caire a déroulé des propositions jugées ambitieuses. Face à ses collaborateurs, le ministre Gabriel Mbairobe a salué l'offre égyptienne, capitale pour la montée en gamme de la destination Cameroun. Il a promis la poursuite des discussions sur ces points mutuellement bénéfiques, dans la droite ligne du renforcement de la coopération Sud-Sud entre Yaoundé et Le Caire. Cet article Tourisme : l’Égypte veut investir au Cameroun est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.description: © DR S’il ne dort pas dans les tiroirs comme d’autres similaires, ce plan est la feuille de route qui va transformer Yaoundé, Douala, Bafoussam, Garoua et toutes les villes camerounaises en villes plus inclusives, connectées et durables. Lancé officiellement le mardi 08 septembre 2026 par le ministère de l’Habitat et du Développement urbain- Minhdu, le ministère des Postes et Télécommunications- Minpostel et ONU-Habitat, le Plan d'action national pour le développement des villes intelligentes est désormais officiel. Il repose sur 3 piliers majeurs présentés comme les axes stratégiques. D’abord la technologie au service de la gestion urbaine. L'idée est d'utiliser le numérique pour régler les problèmes du quotidien : gestion du trafic, collecte des déchets, éclairage public intelligent, sécurisation des quartiers, digitalisation des services municipaux. Fini les files interminables à la mairie pour un acte de naissance. Ensuite l'innovation et l'inclusion sociale. Le Plan vise à ne laisser personne de côté. Il prévoit des services connectés accessibles aux populations, le soutien aux startups locales et aux PME du numérique, et l'implication des universités comme l’Ecole nationale supérieure polytechnique Yaoundé I pour créer des solutions camerounaises aux problèmes camerounais. Enfin, une gouvernance modernisée. C'est le cœur du dispositif. Il s'agit de donner de vrais outils aux Collectivités territoriales décentralisées (CTD). Les mairies et régions ne seront plus de simples spectatrices. Elles deviennent les actrices principales de la transformation, avec un cadre d'intervention clair et des financements dédiés. Ce plan entre en jeu au moment où le Cameroun fait face à une urbanisation accélérée et souvent anarchique. Des villes étouffent en raison des embouteillages, inondations, insécurité, chômage des jeunes. Ce Plan arrive comme une réponse directe au défi climatique pour permettre de rendre les villes plus résilientes aux inondations et à la chaleur grâce à des données et des capteurs. Au défi socio-économique en permettant de créer des emplois dans le numérique et rendre les villes plus attractives pour les investisseurs. Au défi de la décentralisation en donnant aux mairies les moyens technologiques et financiers de gérer leurs territoires. Pour la mise en œuvre du plan dans le volet infrastructurel, le Cameroun s'appuie sur les opérateurs Orange, MTN, CAMTEL ; sur le FEICOM pour le financement des communes ; et sur l'ANTIC pour la régulation numérique. Le PNUD, la Banque mondiale, la Banque africaine de développement, l’Union européenne sont des partenaires qui vont accompagner la mise en œuvre du plan. Cet article Plan national villes intelligentes : ce que le Cameroun va changer dans ses villes est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: KOAFEC : l’IA au centre du nouveau pacte Corée-Afrique
data.description: © DR La 8e Conférence ministérielle de coopération économique Corée-Afrique s'est ouverte le 09 septembre 2026 à Séoul sous le signe du numérique. Thème : "Exploiter l'intelligence artificielle et les infrastructures numériques pour la transformation de l'Afrique". Une quarantaine de pays africains font le déplacement. Séoul veut accélérer son partenariat avec l'Afrique par l'intelligence artificielle. La KOAFEC 2026 a été ouverte par la Première ministre Han Seong-sook, ancienne patronne de Naver, géant technologique coréen. Son gouvernement a fait de l'IA et de la transformation numérique des priorités stratégiques. Coprésidée par le président du Groupe de la Banque africaine de développement, Dr Sidi Ould Tah, et le vice-Premier ministre coréen Koo Yun-cheol, la conférence réunit ministres africains, institutions multilatérales, investisseurs et start-up des deux continents. Pour Dr Ould Tah, qui participe à sa première KOAFEC depuis son entrée en fonction il y a un an, l'enjeu est de repositionner le partenariat dans un monde en mutation. Il défendra la nouvelle orientation stratégique de la BAD articulée autour des Quatre Points cardinaux et de la Nouvelle architecture financière africaine (NAFAD). La NAFAD vise à mobiliser l'épargne africaine, transformer la liquidité du continent en investissements productifs et réduire les risques pour attirer des capitaux internationaux en co-investissement. À l'issue des travaux, une Déclaration finale et un Plan d'action 2027-2028 doivent ouvrir un nouveau chapitre de la coopération Corée-Afrique, misant sur le digital comme levier de croissance. Cet article KOAFEC : l’IA au centre du nouveau pacte Corée-Afrique est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Intégration financière : la BEAC et le PAPSS mobilisent les banques de la CEMAC
data.description: © DR La Banque des États de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC) et le Système de Paiement et de Règlement Panafricain (PAPSS) organisent ce mercredi 9 septembre 2026 un webinaire stratégique pour accélérer l'adhésion des banques de la CEMAC au système de paiement continental. Cap sur la souveraineté financière africaine. Après son adhésion au PAPSS, la BEAC passe à l'offensive pour embarquer les banques commerciales de la zone. Le webinaire de ce mercredi vise à présenter les modalités concrètes de participation, les prochaines étapes de l'adhésion et les opportunités pour le paiement transfrontalier intra-africain. L'enjeu est majeur : fluidifier les échanges, réduire la dépendance au dollar et à l'euro, baisser les coûts et les délais de transfert entre pays africains. Une étape clé de la ZLECAf. Les banques de la CEMAC pourront échanger directement avec les équipes de la BEAC et du PAPSS pour lever les contraintes techniques et réglementaires. Cet article Intégration financière : la BEAC et le PAPSS mobilisent les banques de la CEMAC est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Notation financière : l’Afrique lance sa propre agence pour corriger son risque de crédit
data.description: © DR L'Afrique veut reprendre la main sur son image financière. L'Union africaine a annoncé le lancement officiel le 7 octobre à Maurice de l'African Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA), sa propre agence de notation. Une réponse politique au biais jugé défavorable des agences internationales envers le continent. C'est un acte de souveraineté financière. L'Afrique s'apprête à franchir une étape majeure dans sa quête d'une évaluation plus juste de son risque de crédit. L'Union africaine a annoncé le lancement officiel, le 7 octobre prochain à Maurice, de l'African Credit Rating Agency, AfCRA. Basée à Port-Louis, retenue comme juridiction principale après un processus de sélection conduit sous l'égide du Mécanisme africain d'évaluation par les pairs (MAEP), l'agence est appelée à devenir le porte-voix financier du continent. L'Union africaine avait confirmé dès février que Maurice accueillerait le siège, tout en invitant les autres États à se porter candidats pour des implantations secondaires. Un maillage continental assumé. L'enjeu est politique et économique. Depuis des années, les dirigeants africains dénoncent une surévaluation du risque par les trois grandes agences mondiales - Fitch, Moody's, Standard & Poor's - qui renchérit le coût de l'emprunt pour les États africains et freine les investissements. Avec AfCRA, l'Afrique entend proposer une lecture endogène, ancrée dans les réalités locales, des fondamentaux macroéconomiques et du potentiel de croissance. Une agence africaine pour noter l'Afrique, avec des critères africains. Reste à convaincre les marchés internationaux de la crédibilité et de l'indépendance de cette nouvelle institution face aux géants de la notation. Cet article Notation financière : l’Afrique lance sa propre agence pour corriger son risque de crédit est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Université de Dschang : l’hydrogène vert au cœur d’une conférence sur la souveraineté énergétique
data.description: © DR L'Université de Dschang explore l'avenir énergétique du Cameroun. Réunis le 08 septembre 2026 au Centre de développement du numérique universitaire, chercheurs, décideurs et investisseurs planchent sur "L'avenir de l'hydrogène vert pour un développement énergétique durable". Une conférence DAAD présidée par la Pr Clautilde Mofor, Doyenne de la Faculté des Sciences, qui se tient du 8 au 10 septembre 2026. L'émulation scientifique est en marche à Dschang. La Faculté des Sciences de l'Université de Dschang a ouvert le 08 septembre dernier une conférence internationale dédiée à l'hydrogène vert, vecteur énergétique d'avenir pour le Cameroun. Organisée par le DAAD Service allemand d'échanges universitaires à travers le Département des énergies renouvelables, la rencontre est présidée par la Pr Clautilde Mofor, Doyenne de la Faculté, représentant le Recteur. Elle s'inscrit dans le cadre du réseau des alumni du DAAD qui soutient depuis des années la coopération avec Dschang. Plateforme multidisciplinaire par excellence, elle réunit chercheurs, ingénieurs, décideurs publics, opérateurs privés, investisseurs, étudiants et société civile. Une alliance stratégique au moment où le Cameroun cherche à améliorer l'accès à l'énergie et réduire sa dépendance aux fossiles. Si l'hydroélectricité reste prépondérante, le solaire, l'éolien et la biomasse restent marginaux malgré un potentiel énorme. Le gouvernement déploie des centrales solaires et des solutions photovoltaïques, mais l'instabilité et le coût du thermique freinent l'industrialisation. L'hydrogène vert, produit par électrolyse de l'eau à partir d'électricité renouvelable, apparaît comme la solution : stockable, transportable, reconvertible via piles à combustible pour l'industrie, les transports et le stockage. Le Cameroun a des atouts : fort ensoleillement, ressources hydriques abondantes, façade atlantique, gisements éoliens et biomasse. Restent les défis : coût de production, déficit d'infrastructures, absence de cadre réglementaire dédié. Quatre axes structurent les travaux : matériaux pour le développement durable, production et valorisation de l'hydrogène vert, politiques énergétiques et production durable. La leçon inaugurale a été prononcée par le Pr Tchaya Guy Bertrand, Chef du Département. Le comité local est présidé par le Pr Christian Kenfack Sadem. Cet article Université de Dschang : l’hydrogène vert au cœur d’une conférence sur la souveraineté énergétique est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
